privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: What this site keeps about you, who gets to see it, and how you take it away again.

who.title: Who keeps your data
who.named: {operator} runs this site, decides what happens with what you put on it, and is responsible for it.
who.unnamed: The person who runs this site decides what happens with what you put on it, and is responsible for it.
who.mail: Questions about your data, and the requests further down this page, go to this address:
who.ask: Take questions about your data, and the requests further down this page, to them directly.

what.title: What the site keeps
what.intro: What you put on it yourself, and the little the site needs to work:
what.account: Your account: your name, your email address and when you made it. If you log in with Google, also the number Google knows your account by.
what.lists: Your lists and wishes: their titles, descriptions, links and pictures.
what.giving: What you tick on other people’s lists: which wish, how many, whether you give anonymously, and the notes you write there.
what.visited: Which lists of other people you opened and when you last did, so you find them again under “From others”.
what.sharing: The links you made to share wishes or a list, the ones you used, and the notices about who shares a wish or a list with you.
what.friends: Who your friends are, the requests and friend links you sent or got, which of your lists you show to which friend, and what you sent a friend until they answer it.
what.address: To count wrong passwords and new accounts, the server holds your IP address and the email address you typed in its memory for an hour at most. Neither goes into the database.
what.nothing: Pakske has no statistics, no advertising and no trackers, and keeps no log of the pages you open.

see.title: Who sees what
see.link: Everyone who has the link to a list sees the list, its wishes and the names of its owners, also without an account. Anyone who has the link can pass it on.
see.buyers: Someone who is logged in sees, on other people’s wishes, who is giving what, with names and notes. If you give anonymously, they read “Someone else” where your name would be.
see.owners: The owners of a wish never see who gives it, how many are taken, or what was written about it.
see.picture: A wish’s picture has a random address of its own. Whoever has that address can open the picture.
see.hidden: Other people never see your email address. No page lists the accounts or other people’s lists, nobody sees who opened their list, and search engines are asked to stay out.
see.friends: A friend sees your name and finds the lists you switch on for them. Nobody sees who your friends are. If you ask the owner of a list to be friends, they see your name and which list you asked from. If you decline a request, whoever sent it isn’t told. If you send a friend wishes or a list, they get a notice with your name; if they close it, you aren’t told.

where.title: Where it is kept, and who else is involved
where.server: Everything in the list above is in one database and one folder of pictures, on the server this site runs on.
where.firebase: Logging in goes through Firebase Authentication, a service of Google. Google gets your email address, your name and your password. It keeps the password, and it sends the mails for a forgotten password or a new email address. Google may process this in the United States.
where.passwords: This site keeps no passwords, except for an account from before it used Firebase. That account’s password stays here as a hash, from which the password can’t be read back, until the account next logs in.
where.google: If you choose “Continue with Google”, Google tells this site your name, your email address and the number of your Google account.
where.network: The connection to this site runs through {network}, which sees your IP address and passes on what you send and receive.
where.shops: For a wish with a link, the server fetches the picture that shop shows for it. The shop sees the server, not you. Only when you follow a link yourself are you at the shop.
where.nobody: Your data is not sold, and not passed on to anyone who wants it for purposes of their own.

cookies.title: Cookies and your browser
cookies.intro: The site only sets what it needs to work, so it has no cookie banner:
cookies.login: A login cookie, from the moment you log in. It says which account is yours and holds the key that keeps you logged in at Firebase, sealed so that only the server can read it. It expires 60 days after it was last set.
cookies.opened: While you aren’t logged in, a cookie with the lists you opened, 50 at most, for a year. Logging in moves them to your account and removes the cookie.
cookies.google: During a login with Google, two cookies that remember where you were, for ten minutes at most.
cookies.scheme: Your choice of light or dark, in the storage of your browser. The server never gets it.

why.title: Why the site may use it
why.service: Almost all of it is needed to do what you ask of the site: keep an account, show your lists, and tell buyers what is already taken. Under the GDPR, the European privacy law, that counts as carrying out an agreement with you.
why.safety: Counting wrong passwords and new accounts per IP address protects the accounts and the server. The GDPR calls that a legitimate interest.

keep.title: How long it is kept
keep.until: Until you take it away. You change and delete your lists, wishes, ticks and notes yourself, and you delete your account under Settings.
keep.account: Deleting your account removes it here and at Firebase, with your name and your email address, what you ticked on other people’s lists, your visited lists, your friends and requests, your links and your notices.
keep.stays: Your lists and the wishes on them stay, without your name: anyone who has the link can keep opening them, and nobody can change them any more. Delete them first if you don’t want that. A list you share with someone stays theirs. Your notes on other people’s lists stay too, with “Someone else” where your name was. An account you make later, even with the same email address, gets none of this.
keep.deleted: A deleted list or wish is not erased. It stays in the database, marked as deleted. Whoever had ticked a wish of yours keeps seeing that wish, with your name for as long as your account exists. Nobody else sees it.
keep.erase: Ask whoever runs the site to have deleted lists and wishes erased from the database as well. The same goes for what stayed behind of a deleted account.
keep.backups: Whoever runs the site can make backups. Something you deleted stays in a backup until that backup is replaced.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.self: Most of it you can see and correct on the site itself.
rights.ask: You can also ask for a copy of everything the site keeps about you, have it corrected or erased, or object to how it is used. Ask whoever runs the site. You get an answer within a month.
rights.authority: If the answer doesn’t settle it, you can complain to the data protection authority of your country. In Belgium that is the Data Protection Authority, at dataprotectionauthority.be.

terms.title: Terms
terms.lead: What you can expect from this site, and what it expects from you.

site.title: What this is
site.named: Pakske is a wishlist site that {operator} runs for family and friends. It costs nothing.
site.unnamed: Pakske is a wishlist site that someone runs for family and friends. It costs nothing.
site.agree: By making an account you agree to these terms. A child can have an account when a parent or guardian agrees.

account.title: Your account
account.name: Use a name the others know you by, and an email address you can read: the link for a forgotten password goes there.
account.password: Keep your password to yourself. What happens through your account counts as yours.
account.full: The site has room for a set number of accounts. When that number is reached, nobody new can register.

lists.title: Lists and links
lists.open: A list is open to everyone who has its link, with or without an account, and anyone who has the link can pass it on. You choose who you send it to. An owner can give a list a new link; the old one then stops working.
lists.together: Someone you make co-owner of a list or a wish can change it, just as you can.

content.title: What you put on it
content.yours: Your lists, wishes, pictures and notes stay yours. You allow the site to store them and to show them to the people the privacy page names.
content.rules: Don’t put anything on it that is against the law, that is meant to hurt or harass someone, or that isn’t yours to share, such as another person’s private details.
content.abuse: Don’t try to get into other people’s accounts or lists, and don’t load the site with automated requests.
content.removal: Whoever runs the site can remove what breaks these rules, and close the account behind it.

surprise.title: The surprise
surprise.ask: The site hides from you what others buy for you. It can’t stop you from looking with a second account, so it asks you not to.

giving.title: Giving and buying
giving.tick: A tick is a promise to the other buyers, not an order. The site sells nothing and has no part in what you buy, where you buy it, or whether it arrives.
giving.shops: The links on a wish lead to other sites, and the wish’s owners put them there. Those sites have terms and privacy rules of their own.

asis.title: No guarantees
asis.offered: You get the site as it is. It can be slow or down, it can contain mistakes, and it can stop.
asis.loss: Nothing guarantees that your lists are never lost. Keep a copy of what you can’t do without.
asis.liability: As far as the law allows, whoever runs the site is not liable for damage from using it, unless they caused it on purpose or through gross negligence. Your rights as a consumer stay as they are.

ending.title: Stopping
ending.you: You can stop whenever you like: delete your account under Settings. The privacy page says what goes and what stays.
ending.site: Whoever runs the site can close an account that breaks these terms, and can end the site.

software.title: The software
software.open: This site runs on Pakske, open-source software under the MIT licence. These terms are about this site only. Someone else who runs Pakske sets terms of their own.

changes.title: Changes and questions
changes.date: These terms can change, and the date at the top says when they last did. If you keep using the site after that, the new terms apply to you.
changes.ask: Take your questions to whoever runs the site.
